title: Greetings, Letter Sounds and Objects in the Home
comp: recognize and pronounce basic letter sounds and greet others respectfully

gram.focus: Interjections; personal pronouns (I, you)
box: We say Hi! Hello! Good morning! to greet somebody.
I am happy. You are kind. — I and you are pronouns.

mini: Draw and label one object found in the home (e.g. mat, cup).

sit.t: It is morning. You come into the house and you see Mother. Your friend Bih is with you.
q: What do you say to Mother?
Which things can you see in the house?

l: I am happy to see you.

read.task: Point to each letter. Say the sound. Then say the word.

write.task: Trace the curves, the zigzag lines and the letters B, M, S, D.

l: In my house, I find my mat,
In my house, I find my cup,

integ: Greet three people. Say your name. Name two things you can see in the room.
rubric: greet people at home and at school
say the sounds /b/, /m/, /s/, /d/
name and label one object in the home

title: Naming Objects and Introducing Family Members
comp: identify common home objects and introduce myself and other people

gram.focus: Nouns (common and proper); personal pronouns
box: A noun names a person, a place or a thing: mat, cup, Sam.
Sam and Bih are proper nouns — they start with a capital letter.

phon.focus: Final sounds in monosyllabic words; building 2–3 letter words

mini: Add a name label and a greeting to one home object in the project strip.

sit.t: Your friend comes to your house for the first time. Your family is in the yard.
q: What do you say to introduce your friend?
Who is in your family?

read.task: Read each word. Then read it again, quickly.

write.task: Write these names and nouns: Sam, Mum, mat, bed.

integ: Introduce three people: "This is Mother. She is kind." Then say your own name.
rubric: introduce myself and other people
read 2–3 letter words
write my own name and the names of things at home

title: Polite Expressions and Home Activities
comp: use polite responses and describe simple home routines

gram.focus: Adjectives; interjections (Sorry, Thank you)
box: An adjective tells us more about a noun: a clean cup, a big room.
Interjections are little words we say with feeling: Oh! Sorry! Thanks!

phon.focus: Digraphs ch, sh, th in home words

mini: Add one polite phrase and one home activity to the strip.

sit.t: You are helping Mother. You step on her foot by mistake. Mother is sweeping the floor.
q: What do you say to Mother?
What are you doing in the house?

read.task: Match each phrase to the right picture in your class.

write.task: Trace and write: "Thank you." and "Sorry, Madam."

l: Ngo: Mother, may I help you?
Mother: Yes, my child. Please sweep the floor.
Bih: I wash the cups. We clean together!

integ: Act a small scene. One of you is Mother, one is a child. Greet, help, and say thank you.
rubric: say sorry and thank you at the right time
read and write the digraphs ch, sh, th
describe something with an adjective (a clean cup)

title: Family Routines and Home Description
comp: talk about home routines and describe places and objects

gram.focus: Prepositions of location; simple sentence construction
box: Prepositions tell us where something is: in, on, under, behind.
A sentence starts with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.
examples: The cup is on the table.
The broom is behind the door.

mini: Finalise the strip with a greeting, an object, a polite phrase and a sentence.

sit.t: A visitor comes to your house. She asks where Mother is and where she can sit.
q: What do you say?
Where is your mother? Show her with your hand.

l: The cup is on the table.

i: The cup is on the table.
read.task: Read the sentence. Then show where the thing is.

write.task: Copy and complete: "This is a big ____." "My bed is ____."

l: This is my home. (show the strip)

integ: Show your strip to the class. Say where things are: "The pot is on the fire. The broom is behind the door."
rubric: talk about what my family does at home
use in, on, under, behind
present my Home Strip to the class

title: Naming Places and People in the Village
comp: name familiar places and people in my community

gram.focus: Common nouns; subject pronouns (He, She)
box: We use He for a man or a boy, She for a woman or a girl, It for a place or a thing.
We say capital letters for the names of people: Ngo, Bih.

mini: Draw and label one place found in the village or town.

sit.t: You walk to the market with Mother. You see many people and many places.
q: What places can you see?
Who do you greet on the way?

read.task: Read the word. Point to the place or the person in the picture.

write.task: Trace and write: "shop", "teacher", "nurse".

integ: Point to three places in the picture. Say: "This is the ____. That is the ____."
rubric: name five places in my village or town
use He, She and It correctly
label a drawing of a place

title: Greeting and Describing Community Members
comp: greet people and describe familiar people in my village

gram.focus: Personal pronouns; adjectives (good, kind, strong)
box: Adjectives describe people: a kind woman, a strong man, a tall boy.
He is tall. She is good. They are friendly.

mini: Add a greeting and a short description of a person to the project strip.

sit.t: An old woman is sitting in front of her house. You pass by with your friend.
q: How do you greet her?
What can you say about her?

read.task: Read the sentence. Then say who it is about.

write.task: Copy and write: "This is a kind woman." Then write one sentence about your neighbour.

integ: Describe a person you know: "This is my uncle. He is tall and kind."
rubric: greet an adult politely
describe a person with one or two adjectives
read sentences with He and She

title: Asking About Places and Giving Simple Directions
comp: ask and answer questions about where places and people are

gram.focus: Interrogatives (Where is…?); prepositions in, on, under
box: We ask Where is…? to find a place or a person.
A question ends with a question mark (?).

mini: Add a question or a direction sentence to the project strip.

sit.t: A stranger comes to your village. She is looking for the clinic. Your little sister is sick.
q: What does the stranger ask you?
What do you answer?

l: Excuse me, where is the school?

i: The shop is behind the mosque.
read.task: Read the question. Then read the answer.

write.task: Write a question and an answer: "Where is the ____? It is ____."

l: Visitor: Good morning. Where is the shop?
Child: Good morning. The shop is behind the mosque.

integ: Play the visitor and the child. Ask for the school, the market and the clinic. Answer each time.
rubric: ask Where is…? with a question mark
answer with in, on, under, near, behind
help a visitor find a place in my village

title: Describing Places and Presenting the Strip
comp: describe places and routines in my village or town

gram.focus: Sentence structure; capitalisation and punctuation
box: Start a sentence with a capital letter. End it with a full stop.
With he, she or it, the verb takes -s: He goes. She walks.
examples: he go to the market → He goes to the market.

mini: Finalise the strip with 3 places, a greeting, a person, a sentence and one illustration.

sit.t: Today your class visits the market. Your teacher asks you to describe your village to a visitor.
q: What is in your village?
What do people do there?

l: Father sells food at the market.

i: The nurse is at the clinic.
read.task: Read the text. Then answer: Where does the nurse work?

write.task: Write three sentences about your village. Correct this one first: "he go to the market".

l: This is my village. (show the strip)
My uncle is a farmer. He is strong. (smile)

integ: Present your strip. Say three places, one person and one thing people do there.
rubric: describe three places in my village or town
start sentences with capital letters and end with full stops
present my Village/Town Strip

title: Identifying School Places and People
comp: name common places and people in my school

gram.focus: Nouns (common and proper); subject pronouns (He, She)
box: A proper noun is the name of one person or place: Ngo, Azobe.
A common noun names any person or thing: teacher, desk.

mini: Draw and label one school place or person on the strip.

sit.t: It is your first day in Class 1. You stand at the door of the classroom.
q: What do you say to the teacher?
What can you see in the classroom?

read.task: Read each word. Then point to the thing in your classroom.

write.task: Trace and write: "teacher", "classroom", "desk".

integ: Walk around the classroom with your teacher. Name five things: "This is a desk. This is the board."
rubric: name five things in my classroom
use He, She and It for people and things
label a drawing of a school place

title: Describing School Tools and Actions
comp: describe the tools we use and the actions we do in class

gram.focus: Adjectives; regular verbs in the simple present
box: Verbs tell us what somebody does: read, write, sit, mop.
With he, she, it we add -s: He reads. She writes.

phon.focus: Final sounds in verbs and school items

mini: Add a short action phrase to the project strip.

sit.t: Your teacher asks the class: "What do we do in the classroom?"
q: What do you do in class?
Which tools do you use?

read.task: Read the phrase. Then do the action.

write.task: Copy and write: "I write." "We read." Then write one action you do in class.

integ: Play "What am I doing?" Mime an action. Your friend says: "You are reading."
rubric: name classroom tools
say what people do with -s (He reads)
write one action sentence

title: Greeting, Sharing, and Polite Requests
comp: use polite greetings and requests in the classroom

gram.focus: Modal verbs (Can, May); interjections and conjunctions
box: We use May I…? and Can I…? to ask politely.
We use and to join two ideas: I sit and I read.

phon.focus: Digraphs in social and classroom words

mini: Add a greeting or a request phrase to the project strip.

sit.t: Your pencil is broken. You need to sharpen it. The teacher is writing on the board.
q: What do you say to the teacher?
How do you ask your friend for a pencil?

read.task: Read each sentence politely. Use a soft voice.

write.task: Write two polite sentences: "Thank you." and "May I go out?"

l: Ngo: Good morning, Bih. Can I help you?
Bih: May I borrow your book, please?
Ngo: Yes, you may. Here you are.

integ: Act the dialogue. Then swap. Ask for a book, a pencil and a chair.
rubric: ask politely with May I…? and Can I…?
read and write the digraphs th, sh, ch
share with my friends and say thank you

title: Classroom Routines and Final Presentation
comp: talk about my school day and present my work

gram.focus: Editing simple sentences; punctuation and capitalisation
box: Check every sentence: a capital letter first, a full stop at the end.
With he, she, it, the verb takes -s: She comes.
examples: we sit quiet → We sit quietly.

mini: Finalise the strip with labelled drawings and complete phrases.

sit.t: It is the last day of the theme. Your class has visitors. Your teacher asks you to present your School Day Strip.
q: What do you do every morning at school?
What will you show the visitors?

read.task: Read the sentences in the right order: bell, greet, clean.

write.task: Write three sentences about your school day. Correct this one first: "we sit quiet".

l: This is my school. (show the strip)

integ: Present your strip to the class. Say what you do in the morning, at break and at the end of the day.
rubric: describe my school day in three sentences
correct a sentence with a capital letter and a full stop
present my School Day Strip

title: Naming Occupations and Tools
comp: name common jobs and the tools people use

gram.focus: Common nouns; present tense verbs
box: We say: She is a teacher. He is a farmer.
The verb tells the work: The cook stirs. The driver drives.

phon.focus: Initial sounds in job and tool words

mini: Draw and label one occupation and one tool.

sit.t: You are ill. Mother takes you to the health centre. A woman in a white uniform helps you.
q: Who is she? What is her work?
Which tool does she use?

read.task: Read the word. Then say the job and its tool.

write.task: Write: "The cook stirs." "The driver drives." Then write one job you know.

integ: Play a mime game. Your friend acts a job with a tool. The class says: "She is a nurse. She helps the sick."
rubric: name six jobs
say what job a person does
label a job and its tool

title: Describing What People Do
comp: describe what workers do and where they work

gram.focus: Simple present verbs; prepositions of place
box: The nurse works in the clinic. The driver is on the road.
in, on, at tell us where the work happens.
examples: The cook works in the kitchen.
The driver is on the road.

phon.focus: Final sounds in job and action words

mini: Add one action sentence about a worker.

sit.t: Your aunt sells tomatoes in the market. She works from morning to evening.
q: What is her work?
What does she do every day?

l: The cook works in the kitchen.

i: The nurse works in the clinic.
read.task: Read the sentence. Then say where the person works.

write.task: Write two sentences: "The nurse works in the ____." "The driver is on the ____."

integ: Describe two workers: what they do and where they work. "My father is a farmer. He works in the field."
rubric: say what a worker does
use in, on, at to say where
write two sentences about work

title: Sharing Tools and Speaking Politely
comp: ask politely for tools and talk about duties at work

gram.focus: Modal verbs (Can, May); nouns and adjectives
box: May I borrow the broom? — Yes, you may.
We can describe tools too: a clean mop, an old book.

mini: Add one polite request or greeting related to work.

sit.t: The cleaner wants to sweep the classroom. She needs the broom, but you are holding it.
q: What does she say to you?
What do you answer?

read.task: Read the request politely. Then answer: "Yes, you may."

write.task: Write two polite sentences asking to borrow a broom and a pencil.

l: Cleaner: May I borrow the broom, please?
Child: Yes, you may. Here you are.

integ: Act the scene with the cleaner, the carpenter and the cook. Ask for their tools politely.
rubric: ask for a tool politely
use Can and May correctly
describe a tool with an adjective

title: Reviewing Jobs and Presenting the Strip
comp: talk about jobs and present what people do

gram.focus: Sentence editing; punctuation and pronoun review
box: Check: capital letter, verb with -s, full stop.
she sells food → She sells food. they clean → They clean.

mini: Present the full strip with drawings, phrases and a chant.

sit.t: Your class makes a "jobs wall". Each pupil says what work they want to do when they are big.
q: What work do you want to do?
Why do you like that work?

listen.t: Talking about the work we want
l: I want to be a nurse.

read.task: Read the text. Then answer: Who helps the sick?

write.task: Write three sentences about a worker in your family. Correct this one first: "she sells food".

l: This is a farmer. He plants crops. (show the strip)
This is a nurse. She helps the sick. (point)
I want to be a teacher. (raise hand)

integ: Present your strip with a partner. Each of you describes one job, then answer one question from the class.
rubric: describe two jobs and their tools
correct sentences with capital letters and full stops
present my What People Do Strip

title: Naming Transport and Movement
comp: name types of transport and describe how we move

gram.focus: Common nouns; action verbs in the present
box: We use ride for a bike, drive for a car or bus, walk for our feet.
He rides. She drives. We walk.

phon.focus: Initial sounds in transport and movement words

mini: Draw and label one type of transport.

sit.t: Morning. You must go to school. Your house is far from the school.
q: How do you go to school?
Who goes with you?

read.task: Read each word. Then say how many wheels it has.

write.task: Write: "I walk to school." "He rides the bike." Then draw your transport.

integ: Ask three friends: "How do you come to school?" Answer for them: "Bih walks. Ngo rides a bike."
rubric: name four types of transport
say how I come to school
label a drawing of transport

title: Giving Directions and Describing Movement
comp: give directions and describe where things are on the way

gram.focus: Prepositions on, behind, near, in front; sentence structure
box: We use on for a road, behind for the back, near for close, in front for the front.
Go straight. Turn left. Walk beside the road.
examples: The bus is behind the tree.

mini: Add one directional sentence to the strip.

sit.t: A taxi driver stops and asks you the way to the market. You know the village very well.
q: What does the driver ask?
What do you tell him?

i: The shop is near the mosque.
read.task: Read the direction. Then show it with your hand.

write.task: Write directions from your class to the school gate.

l: Driver: Excuse me, where is the school?
Child: Go straight, then turn left.
Child: No, it is near the big tree.

integ: Draw a simple map. Give your friend directions to the market, the clinic and the school.
rubric: give directions with straight, left, near
use on, behind, near, in front
say where a place is on my map

title: Travel Requests and Safety
comp: ask politely and follow the rules for travelling safely

gram.focus: Modal verbs (Can, May); conjunctions and, then
box: Can I cross here? May I sit near the window?
We use then for the second action: Stop, then look.

phon.focus: Digraphs and blends in safety words

mini: Add one polite travel-related request to the strip.

sit.t: You are standing at the side of a busy road with Mother. Cars and motorbikes pass fast.
q: What must you do before crossing?
What do you say to Mother?

l: May I sit near the window?

read.task: Read the rule. Then show the class what to do.

write.task: Write two safety rules for the road. Start with "Look…" and "Stop…".

integ: Act a road scene in the classroom. One pupil is a driver, others are children. Use the safety words.
rubric: ask politely before crossing or sitting
say three road-safety rules
read safety signs and words

title: Reviewing Travel and Presenting the Strip
comp: talk about how we travel safely and present my work

gram.focus: Sentence editing; punctuation and capital letters
box: they go road → They go on the road. she walk → She walks.
Check every sentence before you present it.
examples: We stop and look before crossing.

mini: Present the completed travel strip with labels, phrases and a chant.

sit.t: Your class makes a road-safety corner. Each pupil presents their travel strip and one safety rule.
q: How do you travel to school?
Which safety rule is the most important?

i: We stop and look before crossing.
read.task: Read the text. Then answer: What do drivers do at signs?

write.task: Write three sentences about travelling safely. Correct this one first: "they go road".

l: This is a bus. (show the strip)
I walk to school with Mother. (point)
Stop and look before you cross! (raise hand)

integ: Present your strip. Say how you travel, one direction and one safety rule.
rubric: describe how I travel to school
say and write safety rules
present my How We Travel Strip
